# This data file gives the list of all the values of x and y that forms a proven palindrome prime of the below form, with x upto 10000. 
#
# Form : N(x,y)=10^x + 10^(x-y) + 12345678987654321*10^(x/2-8) + 10^y + 1 where x is an even number and 1 <= y <= x/2-9.
# Example, For x=40 and y = 3,  N(40,3)= 10^40 + 10^(37) + 12345678987654321*10^(12) + 10^3 + 1 = 10010000000012345678987654321000000001001, a palindrome prime.

# Palindrome primes belonging to this family have x+1 digits. 
# The central core is 12345678987654321 = 111111111^2
# The Palindrome prime numbers are of the form 
# 1<...y-1 zeros...>1<...((x-16)/2-y-1) zeros...> 12345678987654321<...((x-16)/2-y-1) zeros...>1<...y-1 zeros...>1
# Search was performed for members of this family, for values of x upto 10000 to find all admissible pairs of x and y. 
# A total of 3637 primes were found. Of these, 1204 are proven primes. The rest are probable primes.
# The 1204 members were proven with PFGW or by factoring N-1 directly. 
# Data below has the list of proven primes along with the details. All the primes are in all_members_2026-10-05_for_git.txt. 
# There are two large palindrome primes discovered by Serge Batalov with x = 300010 and x = 490030. They are also terms of this family but beyond the searched range.
# Conjecture is that there are infinitely many primes in this family. 

# The list below has 6 columns - first row and explanations are below. 

# Column Header : x   y   digits  v   F_pct    method
# 1st row :       40  3   41      3   7.32     N-1

# Column # - Name      : Description
# ----------------------------------
# Column 1 - x          
# Column 2 - y
# Column 3 - digits    : x+1
# Column 4 - v         : Largest power of 10 dividing N-1, v = min(x, x-y, x/2-8, y)
# Column 5 - F_pct     : 100*v/(x+1): the factored part of N-1 as a percentage of N. F = 10^v = 2^v * 5^v is completely factored.
# Column 6 - method    : Two methods were used. 
#                       BLS75 - using PFGW when F > N^(1/3) or v > x/3
#                       N-1 - factoring N-1 when F <= N^(1/3)
